scenes.tts: How do you put a number on how tightly a protein holds its partner?
scenes.visual: Title fades. A receptor protein and a small ligand drifting near it. On screen: How tightly does it hold on?
scenes.narration: How do you put a number on how tightly a protein holds its partner?

scenes.tts: Binding is never permanent. A protein and its ligand keep joining and coming apart.
scenes.visual: A field of receptors; ligands land, sit a moment, and leave. Some receptors lit (bound), some dark (free).
scenes.narration: Binding is never permanent. A protein and its ligand keep joining and coming apart.

scenes.tts: Write the reaction in the direction it comes apart. The bound complex splits into free receptor and free ligand.
scenes.visual: On screen: RL ⇌ R + L, with the bound pair separating into its two parts.
scenes.narration: Write the reaction in the direction it comes apart. The bound complex splits into free receptor and free ligand.

scenes.tts: The dissociation constant, K D, is the ratio of what is loose to what is bound.
scenes.caption: The dissociation constant, Kd, is the ratio of what is loose to what is bound.
scenes.visual: On screen: Kd = [R][L] / [RL]. The loose pieces highlighted on top, the bound pair below.
scenes.narration: The dissociation constant, Kd, is the ratio of what is loose to what is bound.

scenes.tts: Two concentrations on top and one below leave one. So K D has units of concentration.
scenes.caption: Two concentrations on top and one below leave one. So Kd has units of concentration.
scenes.visual: The units cancel on screen: M × M / M = M.
scenes.narration: Two concentrations on top and one below leave one. So Kd has units of concentration.

scenes.tts: Now pick the ligand level where exactly half the receptors are bound. Free and bound receptor are then equal.
scenes.visual: The receptor field with exactly half lit. Label: [R] = [RL].
scenes.narration: Now pick the ligand level where exactly half the receptors are bound. Free and bound receptor are then equal.

scenes.tts: They cancel. So K D is simply the free ligand concentration at half occupancy.
scenes.caption: They cancel. So Kd is simply the free ligand concentration at half occupancy.
scenes.visual: On screen: [R] and [RL] cross out, leaving Kd = [L] at half occupancy, written Kd = L½.
scenes.narration: They cancel. So Kd is simply the free ligand concentration at half occupancy.

scenes.tts: That makes the scale run backwards. A small K D means tight binding, because little ligand fills half the sites.
scenes.caption: That makes the scale run backwards. A small Kd means tight binding, because little ligand fills half the sites.
scenes.visual: A stickiness scale with an arrow: smaller Kd → tighter binding.
scenes.narration: That makes the scale run backwards. A small Kd means tight binding, because little ligand fills half the sites.

scenes.tts: The most common error is flipping it. Its reciprocal, the association constant, runs the other way. For K D, lower is tighter.
scenes.caption: The most common error is flipping it. Its reciprocal, the association constant Ka, runs the other way. For Kd, lower is tighter.
scenes.visual: Side by side: Kd (lower = tighter) and Ka = 1/Kd (higher = tighter). Banner: for Kd, lower is tighter.
scenes.narration: The most common error is flipping it. Its reciprocal, the association constant Ka, runs the other way. For Kd, lower is tighter.

scenes.tts: Plot fraction bound against free ligand. You get a hyperbola. It rises steeply, then bends over and creeps toward full.
scenes.visual: A hyperbola drawn point by point. Kd marked on the x-axis where the curve crosses one half. On screen: Y = L / (Kd + L).
scenes.narration: Plot fraction bound against free ligand. You get a hyperbola. It rises steeply, then bends over and creeps toward full.

scenes.tts: Oxygen is a gas, so we use its pressure. The dissolved concentration is proportional to the partial pressure.
scenes.visual: A dial linking pressure to dissolved O₂: turn one up and the other rises in step.
scenes.narration: Oxygen is a gas, so we use its pressure. The dissolved concentration is proportional to the partial pressure.

scenes.tts: So for a single site, P fifty, the pressure at half full, is just K D measured in torr.
scenes.caption: So for a single site, P50, the pressure at half full, is just Kd measured in torr.
scenes.visual: The same hyperbola relabelled: x-axis pO₂ (torr); P50 marked where it crosses one half. Label: one site: P50 = Kd in torr.
scenes.narration: So for a single site, P50, the pressure at half full, is just Kd measured in torr.

scenes.tts: Myoglobin is the test case. One chain, one heme, one site. Its P fifty is about two torr.
scenes.caption: Myoglobin is the test case. One chain, one heme, one site. Its P50 is about 2 torr.
scenes.visual: Myoglobin structure beside its hyperbola, P50 ≈ 2 torr marked. Lines at 100 and 20 torr.
scenes.narration: Myoglobin is the test case. One chain, one heme, one site. Its P50 is about 2 torr.

scenes.tts: Predict. Myoglobin is about ninety-eight percent full in the lungs. How full is it at twenty torr, in working muscle?
scenes.caption: Predict. Myoglobin is about 98% full in the lungs. How full is it at 20 torr, in working muscle?
scenes.narration: Predict. Myoglobin is about 98% full in the lungs. How full is it at 20 torr, in working muscle?

scenes.tts: Still about ninety-one percent full. Twenty torr is far above its P fifty, so it barely lets go.
scenes.caption: Still about 91% full. 20 torr is far above its P50, so it barely lets go.
scenes.visual: The 20 torr line meets the curve near the top: about 91%.
scenes.narration: Still about 91% full. 20 torr is far above its P50, so it barely lets go.

scenes.tts: So myoglobin gives up only about seven percent. It is a sponge that grips oxygen and lets go only when oxygen gets truly scarce.
scenes.visual: A thin delivered band between 98% and 91%: about 7%. A sponge icon that stays nearly full until the pressure falls very low.
scenes.narration: So myoglobin gives up only about seven percent. It is a sponge that grips oxygen and lets go only when oxygen gets truly scarce.

scenes.tts: Hemoglobin's curve is not a hyperbola at all. It is an S. The next chapter builds that S.
scenes.visual: The S-shaped hemoglobin curve fades in beside myoglobin's hyperbola.
scenes.narration: Hemoglobin's curve is not a hyperbola at all. It is an S. The next chapter builds that S.

scenes.tts: One site gives a hyperbola, and K D, or P fifty, sets where it sits.
scenes.caption: One site gives a hyperbola, and Kd, or P50, sets where it sits.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: One site gives a hyperbola; Kd, or P50, sets where it sits.
scenes.narration: One site gives a hyperbola, and Kd, or P50, sets where it sits.

scenes.visual: End card. LINE: One site gives a hyperbola; Kd, or P50, sets where it sits.
